newsitem.title: USA: House ethics panel may not have Gingrich report before vote.
newsitem.headline: House ethics panel may not have Gingrich report before vote.

text.p: The House panel investigating ethics allegations against Newt Gingrich may not be ready to disclose its findings until after he has been re-elected as House speaker, a newspaper reported Saturday.

Several Republican House members who supported the Georgia congressman as their party's nominee for speaker in November have said they could rethink their support in a formal vote on Jan. 7 if a pending report by the House ethics investigative subcommittee were unfavourable.

Without any information on the ethics probe, however, the Republicans could re-elect Gingrich only to discover later that his ethics troubles have worsened, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said in an article.

Representative Steven Schiff of New Mexico, one of the subcommittee's two Republican members, told the newspaper a period of confidentiality would follow the conclusion of its work. He apparently was referring to a 30-day period which Gingrich would have under House rules to respond to the report.
"As representatives ourselves, we understand the importance of January 7. But that does not mean we can do everything under our rules to fit with January 7," Schiff was quoted as saying.

Schiff's subcommittee, which consists of two Republicans and two Democrats, has been charged with determining whether the speaker may have violated House rules by involving tax-exempt organisations in partisan political activities.

The Journal-Constitution reported that Gingrich's office got a communication from the House ethics panel Friday. The newspaper said a spokesman for the speaker declined to say whether Gingrich had been notified of the panel's findings.
